newsitem.title: USA: Weekly jobless claims edge higher.
newsitem.headline: Weekly jobless claims edge higher.

text.p: The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits edged higher last week, the government said on Thursday.
The Labour Department said initial jobless claims rose to 309,000 in the week ended Feb. 15 compared with a revised 308,000 the week before.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 323,000 for the week.
The four-week moving average -- seen as a more reliable gauge of trends because it smooths out the often volatile weekly numbers -- fell last week to 318,250 from a revised 325,500 a week earlier.
The department said the four-week average fell last week to its lowest level since the week ended Aug. 17, when it stood at 315,500.
The report included the department's annual revisions to seasonal factors, which affect data going back to 1984.
Total jobless benefit rolls rose by 27,000 to 2.43 million in the week ended Feb. 8, the latest period for which that data were available.
The Labour Department said three states reported increases in initial claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the Feb. 8 week.
They were California with 5,579 additional filings, North Carolina with 2,032 and Texas with 1,278.
California said it had layoffs in agriculture. North Carolina gave no explanation for its increase, while Texas reported layoffs in the service, food and furniture industries.
The department said five states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended Febr. 8, the latest period for which those data were available.
They were Pennsylvania with 2,979 fewer claims, Ohio with 2,506, Iowa with 1,389, New Mexico with 1,172 and Illinois with 1,108.
Pennsylvania reported fewer layoffs in the food, lumber, furniture and electrical equipment industries. Ohio and Iowa gave no reason for the drop in claims.
New Mexico said it had fewer layoffs in the construction, trade, service and mining industries. Illinois reported fewer layoffs in the construction, trade and service industries.
